core_obligations: Set up the analysis on a face of the stability parameter: write the point in the face with its attached dimension vectors and reduce the comparison to the two extremal points of the face, using the author's monotonicity result for the dimension vectors along a wall, which the author attributes to section 5 of the cited paper (proof lines 1021-1150).

The double induction: the proof runs an induction on the rank of the face and on the dimension vector, and the case distinction inside the induction is what produces the successive inequalities for the dimension vectors (proof lines 1021-1150).

The extremal case: at an extremal point of the face the module is a polystable module whose stable components are analysed one by one, and the author's earlier criterion for the non-vanishing of the regular part (label thm:Rudakov) identifies which dimension vectors can occur (proof lines 1021-1150).

The conclusion: the dimension vector of each stable component is bounded by the corresponding face datum, which is the stabilization statement of the lemma (statement lines 999-1019, concluded at the end of the proof).
proof_roadmap: 先把论证化到稳定性参数的一个 face 的两个端点：沿 wall 时维数向量单调，这一条作者引其被引论文第 5 节。
证明对 face 的秩与维数向量做双重归纳；在端点处把模分解成稳定分量逐个分析，并用作者前文关于正则部分非空的判据（thm:Rudakov）认出可能出现的维数向量，最后得到每个稳定分量的维数向量被对应的 face 数据界住。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the face lemma on the stabilization of dimension vectors for zeta-bullet-stable modules (author Lemma at source lines 999-1019, label lem:face), and its proof (source lines 1021-1150) is by far the longest of the paper's second section. The argument is organised as a double induction on the rank of a face of the stability parameter and on the dimension vector, with the reduction to the extremal points of the face relying on the author's monotonicity statement for dimension vectors along a wall, which the author attributes to section 5 of the cited paper (proof lines 1021-1150); at the extremal point the module is decomposed into polystable components and each component is matched against the author's earlier criterion for the non-vanishing of the regular part (label thm:Rudakov). The lemma is the technical device on which the author's later description of the strata rests, and its proof is a genuine multi-step induction rather than a citation. H2.
